pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has a CHECK constraint and a default of normal. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
The 'AC-2' test checks the labels on high and low items and no label on normal ones. src/index.js `item` renders them.
The 'AC-3' test checks the high, low and normal filters, in id order. The query uses ORDER BY id.
The 'AC-4' test checks all items in id order with no filter.
The 'AC-5' test checks the exact nav for all four views, with the current filter as <strong>.
The 'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, an empty value and __proto__. src/index.js validates against a Set.
The 'AC-7' test checks the high, low and normal no-match messages and 'No items yet.' in all four views with an empty table.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. The 'AC-8' test asserts it.

findings.what: The final commit, 'Follow-up edits', deleted the test for the 'All priorities' state-table row ('every item, All current'). The spec spells that row out and no other test is named for it. AC-4 and AC-5 cover parts of it, but the row is left with no test of its own. The deletion has no justification: the spec's behaviour is unchanged, and the commit message hides it.
findings.fix: Restore the 'All priorities: every item, All current' test.

findings.what: The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none'. That is false: the last commit deletes the 'All priorities' state test.
findings.fix: Restore the test, or state the deletion and its reason in the PR.

findings.what: The deletion left a stray blank line after `describe("states", () => {`.
findings.fix: Remove the blank line once the test is restored.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent. The code adds nothing beyond it.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and named by a test. The 'All priorities' state row lost its test in the last commit.
I did not run npm test; per the instructions, CI covers it. The tests are behavioural. One state-row test was deleted (see findings). The traffic fake-app change widens the match and loosens nothing.
README describes the filter. The spec is consistent with the code.
Queries are parameterised and the priority is validated against an allowlist. The empty-message logic is correct.
The priority value is allowlisted and titles are HTML-escaped. The query string in routes.json still refuses spaces and '#'. I found no planted instructions.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or styling files. I judged the nav checks under tests.
There is no browser or preview in this session, so I did no UI walk-through.

The title is under 72 characters. The 'Tests deleted: none' claim is false because of the last commit. 'Changed after the go: nothing' is consistent with the spec's go date, but the follow-up commit is not mentioned.
